details.description: Chirp 3: Instant Custom Voice is a Google Cloud Text-to-Speech feature that clones a voice from a short audio sample and lets that cloned voice be used to synthesize new speech from text. Google's documentation describes providing up to 10 seconds of clean, single-channel consent and reference audio, from which the service generates a text-string 'voice cloning key' that can later be used to synthesize speech. Access is restricted to allow-listed users, who must contact Google's sales team.
advantages: Clones a voice from as little as up to 10 seconds of reference audio, according to Google's documentation.
Supports 25 languages, including multiple English and French locale variants, German, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Russian and several Indian regional languages, per Google's documentation.
Multilingual transfer lets an en-US voice cloning key synthesize speech in German, Spanish, French and Portuguese.
Supports text-based prompting, pace control from 0.25x to 2x speed, pause tags, and custom pronunciation via phonetic encoding.
disadvantages: Access is restricted to allow-listed users and requires contacting Google's sales team, rather than being generally available.
Reference audio must be close to 10 seconds with no background noise, limiting usable source recordings.
use_cases: Personalized audio content creation from a cloned voice
Multilingual voice synthesis from a single voice sample

notes: The docs page's 'Available languages' table names all 25 supported languages explicitly (no '38 languages' figure appears on the page); all of them are listed here. Access is limited-availability (allow-list plus sales contact), not GA, which is called out in the description and disadvantages.
